problem: Existing embodied QA datasets and benchmarks are fragmented, each covering only static perception or isolated skills (spatial grounding, planning) and none model instant, context-aware decision-making or task progress over time.
motivation: Real embodied agents must make instant decisions that depend on spatial layout, temporal progress and task intent, yet current QA resources evaluate only what is visible. A unified, large-scale, decision-oriented dataset plus a strong baseline is needed to train and measure perception-to-decision reasoning in VLMs.
key_idea: Build a 4M+ QA dataset (EQA-Decision) spanning static scene, spatial understanding, task dynamics and instant decision, and train a Qwen3-VL-8B baseline (RoboDecision) with SFT, CoT-SFT and GRPO using a hybrid reasoning/answer/visual-consistency reward.
insight: Ablations show the training stages and data modules are complementary: removing CoT-SFT drops overall score from 68.06 to 54.52 (Temporal Reasoning 52.95 to 31.46), and removing GRPO drops it to 59.85, hurting spatial, grounding and decision. Removing Decision data cuts Instant Decision from 69.93 to 55.84, and dropping Spatial or Task data also hurts it, indicating decisions need combined spatial and temporal cues. Caveat: the benchmark is built with the same pipeline as the training data, so gains are partly in-distribution.
method: Dataset construction: over 4M QA pairs from simulators (HM3D, ScanNet, AI2-THOR/ALFRED), image-QA (Bunny-695K, RoboVQA, RoboPoint), egocentric video (Ego4D, EPIC-KITCHENS-100) and robot data (Open X-Embodiment, AgiBot World), annotated mostly by Gemini-2.5-pro with sampled human verification.

Four modules and nine sub-tasks: static scene (existence/state, counting/location), spatial (depth/direction, grounding/referring, affordance), task dynamics (sub-task planning, state tracking/causality, progress estimation), instant decision (next-action from intermediate frames with context).
Stage 1 SFT: LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on all modules uniformly sampled, vision encoder frozen.
Stage 2 CoT-SFT: about 10% of the data gets Gemini-generated rationale+answer annotations; fine-tune on this subset with the same LoRA setup, warm-starting RL.

Stage 3 GRPO: hybrid reward R = αR_reason + βR_answer + γR_visual with task-adaptive weights; reasoning and answer rewards via E5-large cosine similarity (rule-based for coordinates/boxes/depth), visual reward via OpenCLIP similarity between image and rationale.
EQA-Decision Benchmark: 2,118 held-out samples over six categories, scored by pixel-mask accuracy for grounding and GPT-5 LLM-Match (1-5 mapped to 0-100) for the rest.

setting.training_data: EQA-Decision, over 4M QA pairs (about 10% with Gemini CoT annotations for stage 2), built from simulated, image-QA, egocentric and robot datasets
setting.observation: monocular RGB images / video frames (question-answering setting)
setting.action_space: none (text answers, coordinates and next-action descriptions in QA form)
setting.simulator: HM3D, ScanNet, AI2-THOR used only as data sources; no closed-loop simulator evaluation

numbers.extra: trained on EQA-Decision; 2,118 samples; GPT-5 LLM-Match

results: RoboDecision-8B reaches 68.06 overall on EQA-Decision, versus 51.03 for GPT-5 (strongest baseline), 48.84 for Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and 37.32 for RoboBrain-7B-2.0, winning all six modules. It also beats baselines on RoboVQA, ERQA (54.50) and Where2Place (67.08).
limitations: The benchmark is built with the same annotation pipeline and sources as the training data (Gemini-generated), and is scored by a GPT-5 judge, which risks in-distribution advantage and bias.
Evaluation is offline QA only, with no closed-loop embodied navigation or control, so real decision-making ability is untested.
Benchmark is small (2,118 items) and the reward weights and training details are relegated to the supplement.
